title: Flowchart template and age-group task
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming 2: data structures, files and subprograms
source: Seeded from computing/y10 lesson 9 (Pupil PDF worksheet: flowchart template and age-group task)
intro: Lesson 9: Problem solving core: decomposition, abstraction and algorithms. To understand how decomposition and abstraction turn a real problem into an algorithm shown as a flowchart or pseudo-code

questions.q: Decompose a 'prayer-times reminder' app into four sub-problems.
questions.a: e.g. get location; get today's prayer times; compare with the current time; send a reminder.
questions.model: I do: 1) get the user's town; 2) look up today's five prayer times; 3) check the clock every minute; 4) when a time arrives, show a reminder.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: draw a flowchart and write pseudo-code that inputs an age and outputs 'Child', 'Teen' (13 to 19) or 'Adult'.
questions.a: Two decisions: IF age < 13 → Child; ELSE IF age <= 19 → Teen; ELSE Adult.
questions.model: The teacher draws the first decision: diamond 'age < 13?', yes → output 'Child'.

questions.q: Extend: identify one abstraction you made.
questions.a: e.g. ignored date of birth; used whole years only.

questions.q: Stretch: how many test values would you use, and which?
Breaking a problem into smaller parts is ...
Back to our ponder: How would you explain to a robot how to make a cup of tea? What details could it ignore?
questions.a: Break it into steps (decomposition) and leave out details that do not matter, like the colour of the cup (abstraction).
